findings.evidence: _run_exact_head_review builds a fresh context for the current checkout, but when the stored attempt is terminal it returns status=approved at lines 578-587 before comparing context.head_sha with prior_attempt.identity.exact_head_sha (the comparison begins only at line 588). Thus a task with an approved attempt can commit a new HEAD and receive an approved receipt without reserving or running a review for that HEAD. The focused regression covers only a changed HEAD after changes-requested, so this branch is untested. FinalizationLedger also records approved as the lineage terminal disposition, making the stale approval path the effective behavior rather than a new bounded attempt. This contradicts the exact-HEAD authority boundary and can release unreviewed product bytes.
findings.recommendation: Compare the current HEAD to the terminal attempt identity before returning any terminal result. For a changed HEAD, archive/retain the old attempt as immutable evidence and reserve the next bounded exact-HEAD attempt (or fail closed if policy forbids another cycle), never project the old approval. Add end-to-end regressions for changed HEAD after approved, blocked, and attention-required terminals, including a check that no stale approval receipt is emitted and at most one new provider attempt is reserved.
findings.summary: A terminal approval is reused after the product HEAD changes.

findings.evidence: inspect_callback runs from the ordinary polling loop and, once .review-input.json is stable, calls reserve_callback_submit and immediately executes submit_stable_review_input. reserve_callback_submit in runtime_worker_execution.py:129-138 does not consume a captured provider event; it calls stream.turn_stopped() itself, thereby manufacturing the sole positive ProviderEvent from file stability. The path has no independently observed Stop fact and no process-status guard, so a valid input written while the reviewer is still active—or observed before a dead process is recorded—can authorize callback submission. test_event_only_review_effects.py tests the pure DeliveryController with a manually constructed event but never tests the production event source, while test_callback_submit_recovery_runtime.py stubs reserve_callback_submit and explicitly accepts stable input without an event. This violates the event-only boundary and permits a premature external callback effect.
findings.recommendation: Make callback submission consume a durable, independently captured interactive turn-stopped event bound to the exact generation/process identity. File polling may observe and validate input but must remain zero-effect until that event receipt exists; it must not create the event itself. Add an end-to-end runtime test proving stable valid input before Stop, dead/unknown process, event gaps, and repainted/stable screens produce zero submission, then prove one captured Stop event authorizes exactly one submit and duplicates become typed attention.
findings.summary: Polling a stable review-input file synthesizes the ProviderEvent that authorizes callback submission.

findings.evidence: The baseline identifies e5a8577259fbb59c17ac29e9041bd483197b3a5d, but the repository history and first slice ancestry use e5a8577742d6add41521b2394b56091c0e36dfa5. The required review-inspect facade rejects the documented value as not a local commit. Because config/code-quality-baseline.json copies only aggregate counts and the evidence tests do not validate the subject OID, the baseline production LOC, writable-authority, and incident-literal counts cannot be independently recomputed from the exact tree named by E1. This leaves the mandatory before/after proof unbound even though the final audit is present.
findings.recommendation: Correct the baseline to the actual exact base commit, recompute or independently verify the recorded counts against that commit, and extend the evidence test to require that the subject OID is a local ancestor of every slice and that the baseline metrics match a reproducible audit of that tree.
findings.summary: The E1 baseline names a commit that does not exist, so the claimed reduction is not reproducible from the artifact.
